message.content: {"caption":"Three-stage question-and-answer panel comparing responses about remote sensing and GPS use to protect Amazonian tribal lands.","description":"A text-based comparison diagram. At the top, a blue horizontal bar sits below three questions: “Q1: What kind of sensing technology is being used to protect tribal lands in the Amazon?”; “Q2: What tribe uses GPS devices to map lands?”; and “Q3: Why do some tribes use remote sensing technology?” Below, three groups are labeled vertically at the left as Iter 0, Iter 1, and Iter 2. Each group has an orange vertical bar beside its answers, labeled A1, A2, and A3; thin horizontal lines separate the groups. Iter 0: A1 says, “Drones are being used to map and protect the lands of the tribes in the Amazon.” It has a cross. A2 says, “The Yanomami tribe uses GPS devices to map their ancestral lands in the Amazon rainforest.” It has a cross. A3 says, “Some tribes use remote sensing technology to protect their lands from commercial interests.” It has a check. Iter 1: A1 reads “*model response was empty*” and has a cross. A2 says, “The Kayapo tribe uses GPS devices to map their ancestral lands in the Amazon rainforest.” It has a cross. A3 says, “Some tribes in the Amazon rainforest use remote sensing technology to map out their ancestral lands. This helps them to better protect their territories from commercial interests.” It has a check. Iter 2: A1 says, “The use of remote sensing technology is being used to protect tribal lands in the Amazon.” It has a check. A2 says, “The use of GPS devices by the Trio Tribe, a tribe from the rainforests of southern Suriname, is being used to help protect their ancestral lands.” It has a check. A3 says, “Some tribes use remote sensing technology to protect their lands from commercial interests.” It has a check. The first two answers change from crosses in Iter 0 and Iter 1 to checks in Iter 2; A3 has a check in every iteration.","figure_type":"diagram","chart_values":[]}
